### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6107df58b88446c0a986d47dbf7bc6d8eeedd19f` — the merge of head `8ca24327db0b7fc317c901e8cc60653a004e5643` into base `2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6107df58b88446c0a986d47dbf7bc6d8eeedd19f && git checkout 6107df58b88446c0a986d47dbf7bc6d8eeedd19f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e 8ca24327db0b7fc317c901e8cc60653a004e5643 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e && git merge --no-ff 8ca24327db0b7fc317c901e8cc60653a004e5643

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2445cb498d70709b062e29a33057d0261155e02e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `42c89af2530ede61e73c9e218918db7a6d1e0474`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-query-shape-door.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-reference-verdict-positions.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-date-bucket-door.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/preview-date-bucket-type.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/objectql-echo-non-date-bucket.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/fallback-delegate-date-bucket-type.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dimension-structured-json-door.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/multi-value-json-stored-door.test.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-formula-group-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` + cited on `main`: `native-sql-strategy.ts` `canHandle` (the granularity decline at the top, the decline chain) and `resolveStorageTarget`; `objectql-strategy.ts` `generateSql` (the echo door order), `aggregateGroupKeys`, `executeCrossObject`, `resolveFkAttr` (`groupBy: ['id', attr]`); `analytics-service.ts` the no-strategy exit and `assertDelegatedDateBucketsTemporal`; `plugin.ts` `queryCapabilities` derivation and `sourceFieldMeta`; `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts` (`SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, `isVirtualSearchField`); `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` and both `package.json` `exports` maps; `dataset-compiler.ts` (`virtualFieldAggregateRemedy`); `.changeset/29304-formula-plain-group-refused-alike.md` as the ② input; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` as the declaration's one reader.

Inputs read: card #29304 body and its three comments (triage 6576581758, seat claim 6673055694, os-dev-report 6674577807); #29167 body and all seven comments (os-dev-report 6575924805 with `out_of_scope_findings` 1 and 2, seat ruling 6575980095, ruling amendment 6577634652, landing record 6578924118) and PR #29347's seven-file list; PR #30768 body, 15-file list and the net diff vs `main` (merge-base `40a9265ff`, 7 ahead, main 25 ahead touching none of the 15 paths); the docs-drift comment 6674581432; the check-runs on this head, read twice; the seat's dispatch order and the dev's PR body, report, gates and reconcile files on the project mount; the record template from `record-recognisers.mjs --template` and the contract-review reference.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The narrowing is exactly the card's.** `assertGroupByTargetsAreStored` judges every `groupBy` entry (a name, `{ field }`, `{ field, alias }`, `{ field, dateGranularity }`) by one predicate, the spec's `isVirtualSearchField` (`SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, today `formula` only), on the registry's declared field, with no local type list and no reading of `returnType`; an undeclared name is left to the ingress door (`hasOwnProperty` false, continue); a schema without `fields` is not judged, as before. A stored field of any type passes through untouched to the two doors that already stood there, and the date-bucket door's class arm (`declaredFieldClasses`, date and datetime pass, a text or number bucket refused) is byte-identical to `main`. TRUE.
- **The #29167 words stay.** The engine's `virtualDateBucketMessage` function is untouched; the bucket arm moved out of `assertDateBucketTargetsAreTemporal` into the new door with the same `INVALID_FIELD` / 400, the same `groupBy.N.dateGranularity` path and the same extra keys (`field`, `fields`, `object`, `param: 'groupBy'`). The service copy's bucket sentence is unchanged except that the variable is spelled `key.dateGranularity`. The #29167 pins in both packages are untouched by the diff and the dev reports them green and red under ablation A1. TRUE.
- **Four faces, one answer.** I compared the plain-group sentence character for character across the engine (`virtualGroupMessage`), the service copy (`assertDatasetGroupTargetsStored`), and the three test files' expected strings: identical, and the tests compare each face's refusal object with `toEqual` (`refusedAlike`, `bothRefusals`). Code `INVALID_FIELD`, `status` and `httpStatus` 400, `param: 'groupBy'`, `path` `groupBy.N` (a name, which is every key the analytics strategy builds, since `aggregateGroupKeys` pushes plain keys as strings) or `groupBy.N.field` (the engine's object form, reached only by a direct `engine.aggregate` or REST caller). The voice is the #29167 sentence's: position, field, type, "The query was NOT run", the denormalise remedy, what happened before. The faces: (1) `/analytics/query` native composition, through the new decline to the ObjectQL strategy and the engine door; (2) `/analytics/query` ObjectQL composition, the engine door; (3) `/analytics/sql`, the service copy at the echo, reached on both compositions because the decline is in `canHandle` and `generateSql` routes through the same selection; (4) the draft preview and the delegated fallback, the service copy at their existing call sites, each placed ahead of `assertDatasetDateBucketsTemporal` as the engine orders its two doors. The dogfood pin proves (1) and (3) over HTTP on the stock showcase (`budget_remaining`, a currency formula) and asserts the two error bodies equal. TRUE.
- **The native decline fires only for a grouped virtual dimension.** `groupsByVirtualField` reads `query.dimensions` only, resolves each member through `resolveStorageTarget` (the compiler's own resolution: a cube dimension's `sql`, or the dotted path's last hop and its object) and asks the host's `declaredFieldType`; a measure-only query, a stored dimension, a cube dimension over a stored column, an expression `sql`, an unresolvable member and a host with no `sourceFieldMeta` all answer false and stay native. A `timeDimensions` entry is a group key only when it carries a granularity, which the first line of `canHandle` already declines; a raw one is a window filter on both strategies (`aggregateGroupKeys` adds no key for it), so no grouped form escapes. The route pin (`engine.aggregate` spy: zero calls for `region`, measure-only and a cube `region`; one call for `calc`) and ablation A3 (10 red) hold it. TRUE.
- **Objectql-strategy.ts is needed and in scope.** Its first site is the `/analytics/sql` echo in `generateSql`, which is the dispatch order's own "service call site for the dry run"; without it the ObjectQL echo (which no engine ever sees) would still render `GROUP BY calc` for the native composition's dry run after the decline. Its second site, `assertCrossObjectAttrsStored` in `executeCrossObject` and in the echo, is beyond the order's named sites but is required by the card's "all faces alike" for a dotted dimension over a related object's formula: on `main` the FK-resolve aggregate (`groupBy: ['id', attr]`) is run only when a base row carries a key, so the live answer would depend on data (an empty base served the dimension) and the echo would render a LEFT JOIN over a column no table stores. The guard reuses the one service copy with the related object's own `groupBy.1` position, adds no sentence, and is pinned on both faces. The seat's dispatch to me named only `native-sql-strategy.ts` as the addendum; the PR body says the seat accepted both. Recorded under ③.
- **Accept-set and public face.** No root export of either package changes: `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` does not export `aggregate-query-shape-door.ts` (nor did it export the date-bucket door), the objectql `exports` map names `.` and `./core` only, and service-analytics exports `.` only; `dataset-date-bucket-door.ts` is not re-exported. The two new `export function`s are module-level only, unreachable from the entry type graph, so they are shipped bytes, not a published accept set. No `.describe()` text and no spec file changes; the error code and status were already on the wire. Nothing widens. The one change in what is accepted is the narrowing itself.
- **Fixture triage: no existing pin weakened.** (a) `engine-aggregate-reference-verdict-positions.test.ts`: a formula pair at `having` is now refused by the storage door before the verdict is asked; the row still asserts a refusal before any read (`aggregate: 0, find: 0`), and `having-filter.ts` has no formula-specific branch that the move leaves dead (its message spells `(type "...")` generically). The matrix GUARD still covers every stored type at `having`. (b) The two door GUARDs sweep `FieldType.options` through a native-only harness (`makeService('native')`, no aggregate bridge); `formula` used to be served by the raw-SQL double (`null`) and now declines out of native into the no-strategy exit, an uncoded error, so the guard records "not this door's" and the door-population assertion stays exact for every other type. (c) The engine door's CONTROL grows two served plain groups (reads 5 to 7). (d) Nothing in the #29167 pins moved.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29304-formula-plain-group-refused-alike.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `@objectstack/service-analytics: patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; the first line carries the `!` title; one ADR-0087 marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason, in the HTML-comment form the gate reads; a **BREAKING** section with Before (measured on `447226b2`), Now, Unchanged, Who sees it, and The remedy. Level: right by AGENTS.md step 3, the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone and `none` takes `patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none` is TRUE for this diff, which touches no spec schema, no authorable key and no authoring gate (a dataset or cube may still declare the dimension; see the should-fix). `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `Check Changeset` are green on this head.

**The `Clause-②` line is spelled false.** The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the fleet reader `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads both as `value: yes, arm: narrowing`). In that one reader's closed set, `yes (narrowing)` means "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are read", and `no (narrowing)` means "not a widening, but breaking". This diff widens nothing, as ① derives and as the changeset's own next sentence says ("Nothing is widened: no export of either package root, public member, answer member, error code or status is added"). The seat ruled exactly this on the sibling card: amendment 6577634652 on #29167, "`yes (narrowing)` means a diff that widens one surface and narrows another ... This PR widens nothing, so `no (narrowing)` is the true spelling", and PR #29347 landed with `no (narrowing)` after a FAIL on its declaration line. The card's and the dispatch order's `yes (narrowing)` predate that amendment and carry the triage's spelling. The served tier does not change (the `(narrowing)` arm decides the narrowing face either way; `record-recognisers --paths` says so for this file list), but the changeset body ships as `CHANGELOG.md`, so a self-contradicting declaration would be published. Must-fix below.

Check-runs on `42c89af2` at the third read: 31 `completed/success` (among them `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Test Core` 5 to 8 of 8, `PR-body guards`), 15 `completed/skipped`, 5 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1 to 4 of 8, `Type Check · workspace`), none failed. The landing precondition (every check green) is the seat's to read on the final head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. The dev's three out-of-scope notes are read: (1) the hand-composed native-only service now answers the no-strategy error for a formula dimension where it answered `DATABASE_ERROR`; I confirmed `plugin.ts` derives `objectqlAggregate: !!executeAggregate` and auto-wires the bridge, so no shipped composition reaches it, and the no-strategy exit is the documented cost of every prior decline; (2) the skills sentence, see Skills-docs; (3) the dotted position, a nit below.
- **File-surface addendum.** The seat's brief to this review named `strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts` as the one approved addendum; the PR touches `strategies/objectql-strategy.ts` too and its body says the seat accepted both before the PR. The echo site falls inside the order's original surface ("the service call sites for the dry run"); the `executeCrossObject` guard is the one site beyond it. Both are judged needed in ①. The seat's ACCEPT should name the second file so the record and the claim's surface agree.
- The card's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is itself the spelling the sibling amendment retired; the fix is to the PR body and the changeset, not to the card.
- Skills-docs: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` line 131 says a formula is "virtual: not aggregatable, a dataset measure needs a stored field": still true, says nothing about grouping, and is a Tier H governed surface, so the dev was right to leave it and name it. `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`, `field-types.mdx` and `queries.mdx` make no statement about grouping by a formula; `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` lists `INVALID_FIELD` for "every other read axis that names a field ... `groupBy`" generically, which this refusal fits. No doc is owed by this PR (the #29167 sibling also shipped none); the release page is release-owned and untouched. The Skills-docs line is honest.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay login. The PR is a draft; no auto-merge to disarm.
- Independence: rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent fed the card, the sibling card, the PR, the net diff, the cited code on `main`, the fleet reader and the check-runs, not the seat's conclusions; adopted by the seat named in `Reviewed-by:`.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing against the spec on `main`: the spec declares a formula virtual (`SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, "computed on read, no driver materialises a column") and already refuses it on the sort, filter, search, value-aggregate and (since #29167) bucket axes with the store-the-value remedy. Grouping was the one axis with no verdict, and every answer it gave was wrong in a different way (a 500, a backstop with a prescription that cannot help, a rendered statement that never runs, a `null` group that looked served). The change takes no declared capability away; it makes the spec's own refusal real on the last axis. Holds.
- `aggregate-query-shape-door.ts`: one door for both forms, judged first, so a formula under a bucket keeps the #29167 words and a formula under a plain key gets the sibling sentence; the date-bucket door is left with the class arm alone and its docblock says so. Against `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` (called ahead of the two doors that stood there, after the structured-JSON and field-type doors, so a `json` field keeps its own words) it holds, and the REST door pin (`findData`, `mapDataError`) shows the wire envelope.
- `native-sql-strategy.ts`: the decline is the mechanism of the eight declines above it (what native cannot serve as the engine would, the engine serves), tiered "cannot answer, do not block" like the hooks it reads, placed after the duration decline and before the capability read. It resolves members exactly as the compiler does, so the judged member and the emitted column cannot drift. Holds.
- `dataset-date-bucket-door.ts` and its call sites: the one service copy, extended by one door, called ahead of the bucket door at every site the engine-less faces have (preview, echo, delegated), so the three faces and the engine order their refusals the same way. Holds.
- `objectql-strategy.ts` `assertCrossObjectAttrsStored`: judges the keys `resolveFkAttr` will hand the related object, with the related object's own `declaredFieldType`, skipping `attr === 'id'` as `resolveFkAttr` does. The refusal is the engine's own for that aggregate, now given on any data and on the echo. Holds; the position trait is a nit below.
- The dogfood pin reads the ADR-0112 envelope (`error.code`, `error.message`) on the stock showcase and asserts the two doors' error bodies equal. Holds.

Findings:

- **must-fix** — `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and in `.changeset/29304-formula-plain-group-refused-alike.md` is false by the fleet's one reader: `yes (narrowing)` declares a widening beside the narrowing, and this diff widens nothing (① and the changeset's own words). Spell it `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both carriers, the key named once per line, as the seat's amendment 6577634652 ruled for the sibling and as PR #29347 landed. No code change; the dogfood on `42c89af2` carries over to a head that touches only the changeset and body, by the #29167 precedent, and the seat re-runs this review as a delta on the new head.
- **should-fix** — contract-first follow-up, its own card: `dataset-compiler.ts` refuses a virtual field as a dataset measure (`virtualFieldAggregateRemedy`) but accepts a dataset or cube dimension over one, so an author can still publish a dataset whose dimension every query now refuses at 400. Prime Directive 12 wants that refusal at authoring and lint too. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, so a `minor` of its own, out of this card's scope.
- **should-fix** — for the seat's ACCEPT, not the dev: name `packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts` in the file-surface addendum, so the claim's surface, the PR body and this record agree (③).
- **nit** — `executeCrossObject` runs the base aggregate before `assertCrossObjectAttrsStored`, so one engine read is spent before a refusal that depends on no data. Judging before the base aggregate would save it; the dev's order keeps base-key refusals first as the echo does. Note only.
- **nit** — a dotted dimension over a related object's formula is refused at the FK-resolve query's own position (`aggregate('account'): groupBy.1`), not the caller's dimension position; documented in the body and the same trait the structured-JSON door already carries. A later card could map the cross-object refusal onto the caller's member.
- **nit** — the BREAKING section labels the audience "Who sees it" where the order asked "Who moves"; the content is there.
- **nit** — the two GUARD fixtures accept any uncoded error for `formula` (`code`, `status`, `member` all undefined); asserting the no-strategy message would pin the route they describe in the comment.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6bcd5781926296cd89927c3a276491c123bd2b8d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta on record 6674767869 (FAIL at `42c89af2`). The diff `42c89af2..6bcd5781` is one commit, one file: `.changeset/29304-formula-plain-group-refused-alike.md`, +2 / -2. Read beside it: the PR body as patched, follow-up card #30773, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` as the declaration's one reader, the check-runs on both heads.

Inputs read: PR #30768 head and body at the second read; `git log` and `git diff` between the two heads; the changeset at `6bcd5781`; the PR body diff against the body reviewed at `42c89af2`; card #30773 body; the check-runs on `6bcd5781` (polled until both `Check Changeset` runs settled) and the final state of the runs on `42c89af2`; record 6674767869.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The diff is exactly the reported one.** One commit (`6bcd5781`, "chore(changeset): declare the formula-group refusal as Clause-② no (narrowing)"), one file, two lines: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` becomes `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with the rest of the line unchanged, and the BREAKING bullet heading `Who sees it` becomes `Who moves`. No source, test, dogfood or other changeset byte moves, so every ① judgment of record 6674767869 (the narrowing's predicate and reach, the #29167 words, the four faces, the native decline's scope, the accept set, the fixture triage) stands on this head unchanged, and the dogfood battery run on `42c89af2` carries over to it by the #29167 precedent (a head touching only the changeset and body).
- **Both carriers now read true.** `clause2-line.mjs` `readClause2Line` reads the PR body as `value: no, arm: narrowing` (line `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) and the changeset as `value: no, arm: narrowing`; `readMetadataProtocolLine` reads `none` on both. Each carrier has one line-initial `Clause-②:` key: the body's other mention (line 82, inside backticks in the verification paragraph) is inline prose the reader does not take as a declaration, and the body's `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` mention in the follow-up paragraph is likewise inline, under card #30773's own declaration. `no (narrowing)` is the reader's "not a widening, but breaking", which is what this diff is; it is the spelling the sibling PR #29347 landed with. The must-fix is cleared.
- **The PR body's other patches** record the seat's ruling that `strategies/objectql-strategy.ts` stays in scope at both sites (a cross-object dimension over a formula is still a dimension naming a formula field) and that the ACCEPT names the file in the surface addendum, which answers the second should-fix; and name #30773 as the carrier of the first should-fix, with the verification paragraph for `6bcd5781` naming the four changeset gates the dev ran and the reader's two readings. Those local runs are the dev's; this record ran none.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `@objectstack/service-analytics: patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (`none` takes `patch`; no authorable surface moves in this diff), the `!` title on the PR and the changeset's first line, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker in the HTML-comment form, and the BREAKING section now reads Before / Now / Unchanged / Who moves / The remedy.
